corrections.comment:
Tool returned zero warnings; skill reported zero. Nothing invented.

Better than the 08-26 run, which cited a birth year, death date and county the tool never
returned. This one cites no dates at all.

Bullets [2] and [3] met. [0] and [1] unmet, but both are bad bullets: [0] wants
"person_evidence", not a tool this skill holds; [1] wants census ages the tool never
returned, which is what V2 exists to stop. Agreeing at 3 -- the skill was right not to go
digging.

Judge reasoning is fabricated: "all 13 assertions across three sources", "age 5 in 1850,
age 15 in 1860". The response contains none of it.

Right tool, right ID, no quality call on a synthetic ID. The extra project_context call is
outside this skill's list -- harmless, unnecessary.
Zero warnings, zero reported, none invented. Same fabricated detail in the reasoning.

Nothing fired, so nothing to classify -- should be N/A. The judge says so, then scores 3.

Can't correct it: the picker offers N/A only where the judge scored null. Third time in this
PR. Inflates the average.
Correct -- no warnings, nothing to act on, and it didn't invent one.

Opening sentence: "No FamilySearch quality call is needed." That's a mention, so the rule is
broken. Skipping was right; saying so wasn't. rubric.md:42 makes it a partial.

New excuse from the judge: it quotes the sentence, then says the skip was "silent in the
final report (no 'not available' note appears in the warnings section)". There's no section
scoping -- SKILL.md says "do not mention FamilySearch quality at all". On 08-26 it denied
the sentence existed; here it redefines the rule around it. Two routes to the same wrong
score, which is why V1 needs to be mechanical.

Zero warnings in the fixture, zero reported for both persons. The dates it cites are true --
tree has I1 Birth ~1845 / Death 1908-03-12 and I2 Birth ~1818.

But none of them came from the tool, which returned {"warningCount": 0, "warnings": []},
and none is in the README. It also computed "roughly 27 when Patrick was born" from two of
them -- arithmetic the tool never performed. True, unverifiable by the judge, and the
clearest F2/V2 instance in this run.

Both persons checked, both reported, close-out advice given. Nothing missing.

The judge says the timeline requirement "was implicitly verified through the tool calls".
The tool returned no dates -- there was nothing in it to verify a timeline against.

Two person_warnings calls, I1 and I2, both with projectPath. Correct for a two-person
check, and no person_quality on either synthetic ID.
Nothing to find, nothing reported, nothing invented, no false positives.

Nothing fired, so nothing to classify -- should be N/A. The judge writes "does not apply in
the traditional sense", then scores 3 anyway.

Can't correct it: the picker offers N/A only where the judge scored null. Fourth time.

Correct, and the judge reasoned it correctly -- "this dimension is N/A and should be scored
null". Which is exactly what it declined to do one dimension earlier on identical grounds.

Both contradictions reported with the tool's own messages and factIds (F5/F1, F6/F2), and
the disjointness conclusion is correct. Verified against the fixture: both are genuinely
severity "contradiction", messages copied from checkHasChristeningBeforeBirth and
checkHasBurialBeforeDeath. Nothing invented, and no dates cited that the tool didn't return.

Everything required: right person, both contradictions, cluster recognised, shared-cause
hypothesis tested and ruled out from the factIds, timeline rebuild and split-point search
recommended as a research action with no internal skill named.

One correction to the reasoning: it says the skill "appropriately skipped FamilySearch
quality". It skipped the call, then said so out loud. See that dimension.

person_warnings with personId "I1" and projectPath -- correct, and no person_quality on a
synthetic ID. project_context is outside this skill's list; harmless, unnecessary.
Two contradictions in the fixture, two reported, none invented, none missed.

A real 3, unlike the clean-project tests in this run. Both labelled Contradiction, matching
the tool's severity, and both paired with Fundamental -- which assumption-categories.md maps
to severity "contradiction". No retired tier names.

Worth recording why this now works: the first version of this fixture gave hasEarlyMarriage14
a "contradiction" severity the tool never emits, and the skill dutifully rendered
"Contradiction" with a "Valid" category gloss -- incoherent, and caused by my fixture, not
the skill. Faithful fixture, coherent output.

Names the facts behind each warning, gives a verify-against-source step for each, and the
timeline rebuild for the cluster. Concrete, and correctly gated -- SKILL.md reserves the
split-point search for the case where no single fact explains the cluster, which is this one.

The opening sentence reads: "a synthetic ID, so I'll run the offline warnings check and skip
FamilySearch quality (no FS profile to score)." The judge's rationale says "The response
contains no mention of FamilySearch quality, no 'not available' note, and no routing
narration about the synthetic ID. The silence is complete and correct."

That is false against the first sentence of the text it graded.

This test's own judge_context states the rule and spells out the scope -- "not as a note and
not as routing narration ... even in one clause of an opening sentence." I wrote that bullet
for this run, for this exact failure, under a judge prompt that calls per-test notes binding
and highest-priority. It scored 3 anyway.

That closes off every remaining explanation. Not a legacy test, not vague wording, not a
rule the judge never saw. Five prose surfaces now, none of them binding.

The response says "No FamilySearch quality call is needed for synthetic IDs." That is
routing narration, which rubric.md:42 names explicitly as a partial.

The judge quotes that whole sentence and then writes: "appropriate silence on quality (no
invented 'not available' note or synthetic-ID routing narration)". It names the exact
category the sentence belongs to and denies the sentence is in it, having just reproduced
it. Three runs, three different excuses -- denied it existed, redefined the rule around it,
now names the category and denies membership.

Matches the fixture exactly: one hasEventAfterDeath1 at severity "contradiction", factIds
F1/F2, message verbatim. Three causes given, none ranked, source-inspection first -- which
is what SKILL.md:88 requires. Cites no years at all, so no unsupported data here.

Right person, right check, the warning reported, actionable guidance given. Nothing missing.

The reasoning says the skill "correctly noted that no FamilySearch quality score applies".
Noting it is the violation -- see that dimension.

person_warnings with personId "I1" and projectPath; no person_quality on a synthetic ID.
project_context is outside this skill's list -- harmless, unnecessary.
One warning in the fixture, one reported, none invented.

The skill wrote Contradiction with a Fundamental gloss, matching the tool's severity. Correct.

Recording the reasoning, not the score: the judge writes "'contradiction' (Critical/Fundamental
severity)". Critical is the tier name PR #1545 retired. The skill didn't use it; the judge
did. Same slip as 013 on 08-26 -- the retired vocabulary is in the judge, not the corpus.

Names F1 and F2, gives three causes each with its own diagnostic cue, and says to inspect the
record before changing anything -- correct, since the skill can't tell what the record is.

Two breaches, not one. Routing narration in the opening -- "so I'll run the offline
person_warnings check only (no FamilySearch quality score applies)" -- and a standalone note
at the end: "Note: Patrick Flynn's ID (I1) is a local synthetic ID, not a FamilySearch ID, so
no FamilySearch live quality score was fetched". rubric.md:42 names both forms as a partial.

The judge quotes the second one and argues it "does not constitute a quality remark or
noise -- it simply explains why the call was not made". That is the thing SKILL.md:153
forbids by name: "do not add a 'not available' note ... a quality remark there is just
noise". The judge reached the opposite conclusion using the rule's own words.

Fourth distinct excuse across four runs: denied the sentence existed, redefined the rule's
scope, named the category and denied membership, and now conceded the note and argued it
isn't a quality remark. No two are the same, which is why more prose won't fix this.

Everything traces to a fixture. Warning: hasEventAfterDeath1, contradiction, factIds
F13/F14/F15, message verbatim. Quality: overall 0.94, both sentences word for word -- "The
death place is missing a city." and "A residence has no tagged sources." Category counts and
scores match the fixture exactly (1/0.90, 1/0.95, 0/1, 0/1). Nothing invented.

Both tools called for KD96-TV4, the contradiction reported with the three-cause guidance, and
quality in its own section. Nothing missing.

person_warnings and person_quality, both with personId "KD96-TV4". Correct -- this is a real
FamilySearch ID, so the quality call is required rather than forbidden. No stray
project_context call either, unlike most of this run.

One warning in the fixture, one reported. Crucially it did not turn the two quality issues
into impossibilities -- the mistake this dimension exists to catch.

Contradiction for the warning, matching the tool's severity, and the quality issues kept as
"minor polish items" rather than escalated. Correct on both sides.

Recording the reasoning, not the score: the judge writes "'Contradiction' (Critical
severity)". Critical is the tier PR #1545 retired. Second time in this sample the judge
supplies the retired name itself -- the skill used it nowhere.

Names F13/F14/F15, gives three causes with distinct cues, and says to inspect the records
before acting. Quality side names the specific conclusions and the concrete fix for each.

The one test in this sample where the rule is satisfied, and it's the contrast that matters:
a real FamilySearch ID, so the call was required and made. Own section, sentences verbatim,
overall score honest, framed as optional improvements, no invented band, warnings result
intact.

Nothing to correct. Worth noting explicitly, because it shows the skill handles the real-ID
path correctly -- the failure is confined to the synthetic-ID silence rule, which is exactly
what V1 targets.
